section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1971
title: 6 1970 to 23,255 during 1971, while deaths on roads had indicated a sharp increase from 7,288 deaths during 1970 to 11,740 during 1971. The pattern of percentage distribution of accidental deaths due to various causes has slightly changed from that of 1970. Accidents on road accounted for 11·1% of the deaths during 1971 as against 5·2% during 1970. Similarly, railway accidents accounted for 9·1% of the total accidental deaths during 1971 as against 5·9% during 1970. Fire constituted 9·3% of the total deaths during 1971 as against 6·7% during 1970 while for other causes there has not been a significant difference. Table 2 indicates the number of accidental deaths during the last 8 years viz., 1964 to 1971. The incidence shows a consistent increasing trend up to the year 1970 but during 1971 there was a sharp decrease, the decrease being 24·4% during 1971 over 1970. The volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population had been fairly consistent during the period 1966 to 1970 and it remained more or less 24 during this period. During 1971, it had decreased sharply and was only 19·2.
